title: JWT Integration
description: Use JWT tokens for authentication in GraphQL.

data.text: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are the most common way to authenticate GraphQL clients. The client sends a bearer token in the Authorization header, and Hot Chocolate validates it via ASP.NET Core.
Create a mutation or endpoint that generates a JWT after validating the user's credentials.

data.title: Generate JWT
data.content: Create a login mutation that returns a token.

data.text: Clients store the token (usually in localStorage) and send it in the Authorization header on every request.

data.title: Client Request
data.content: Send JWT in the Authorization header.

data.title: Token Security
data.text: Always use HTTPS. Store JWTs in httpOnly cookies for web apps to prevent XSS. Set reasonable expiration times and use refresh tokens for long-lived sessions.

terms.definition: JSON Web Token — a compact, signed token that carries identity claims.
A token presented in the Authorization header as "Bearer <token>".
A long-lived token used to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Clients send tokens in Authorization header
Use refresh tokens for better UX
data.takeaway: Next, we'll integrate with ASP.NET Core Identity.
